findings.title: Task 12 (ConsistencyChecker test) is scope creep — no production code path requires it, and the slice design explicitly scopes it out
findings.description:
The slice design's **Scope / Out of scope** section states: *"Any change to `ConsistencyChecker.ts` rules beyond the arithmetic effect of Decision 3 flowing through automatically … No new `ConsistencyChecker` rule is being added for `[~]` entries specifically."* Decision 3 already makes `completedSlices` count deprecated entries as resolved, so `allComplete = completedSlices === totalSlices` is satisfied purely through the parser change — no `ConsistencyChecker` test is needed to verify a code path that the design says needs no change.

None of the seven success criteria in the slice design ask for a `ConsistencyChecker` regression test. The closest criterion — *"`ConsistencyChecker`'s `plan-status-vs-entries` / `arch-status-vs-plans` rules do not false-positive when a plan's frontmatter is `status: complete` and its only non-checked entry is a `[~]` deprecated one"* — is a *behavioral guarantee*, not a *test-task mandate*. The design treats it as an automatic consequence of Decision 3, not as a work item. Task 12 converts an automatic consequence into a dedicated two-case test task, which is a test beyond what the success criteria require.

This is the proportionality concern flagged in the review brief: a test task whose asserted behavior the design says is already covered by the arithmetic change, with no implementation task pointing at `ConsistencyChecker.ts`. It also risks an over-specified, brittle assertion (the "complementary case" requiring `plan-status-vs-entries` to *fire* for `status: in-progress`) that the design never asks for.

Cut Task 12, or fold its first case into the full-verification pass (Task 13's manual walkthrough step 5 already covers the "frontmatter `status: complete` + only `[~]` entry → no finding" path). Do not add a production-code task for it — there is none to add.

findings.title: Tasks 1–13 sequencing and test-with pattern are sound; the regex-widening + status-setting + arithmetic change are correctly one logical parser change split for traceability
findings.description:
Cross-referencing the seven success criteria against the tasks: every criterion has a covering task.
- "indexed `[~]` parses to `status:'deprecated'`, `isChecked:false`, description captured" → Tasks 1, 2, 3, 5.
- "unindexed `[~]` parses equivalently with fallback index" → Tasks 1, 2, 3, 5.
- "`totalSlices` includes it; `completedSlices` counts it as resolved" → Task 4 (and asserted in Task 5's `totalSlices:7, completedSlices:5`).
- "`cf list slices` renders `⊘ deprecated`, never `← next`" → Tasks 8, 9, 10.
- "`cf next`/`findFirstNotCompleteEntry` skip a `[~]` entry with no design/task" → Task 11 (verify-only, correct given `findFirstNotCompleteEntry` already excludes `STATUS.Deprecated`).
- "ConsistencyChecker rules don't false-positive" → addressed by Decision 3's arithmetic (automatic); Task 12 is the questionable extra, see above.
- "existing `[ ]`/`[x]`/`[X]` byte-identical (regression-free)" → Task 5's explicit regression assertion.

Sequencing is correct: fixture (Task 1) precedes parser change (Tasks 2–4) so the "before" state is observable, per the CLAUDE.md lenient-parsing rule; each implementation task is immediately followed by its test task (2–4 → 5; 6 → 7; 8–9 → 10; 11 and 12 are verify-only). `**Commit**:` markers sit at tested points after Tasks 5, 7, 10, 11, 12, and the final verification pass — not after every task and not only at the end, consistent with the rule. No circular dependencies: Task 8 depends on 6 (signal field) and 3 (`entry.status`); Task 9 depends on 6 and 3; Task 10 depends on 8–9; Task 11 depends on 8. All satisfiable by a junior AI with the cited file:line anchors.

The 13-task count is at the upper end but justified: this slice touches four production files across two packages plus three test files, and each task is narrowly scoped (single regex class, single field, single call-site). No task is too large; none is so granular it should be merged. The only proportionality issue is Task 12 (above).
